newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Diplomats in Maputo angry at murder of Swiss woman.
newsitem.headline: Diplomats in Maputo angry at murder of Swiss woman.

text.p: The murder of a Swiss woman in Mozambique nine days ago has led to foreign diplomatic pressure on President Joaquim Chissano's government to take serious measures to curb a wave of violent crime.
The heads of many foreign diplomatic missions met at the Swedish embassy in Maputo on Monday to discuss an alarming recent rise in violent crime and the failure of the police to catch the culprits.

The deputy director general of the Swiss Cooperation Office, Rudolf Dannecker, has been in Maputo since Sunday to discuss the implications of the murder with the Mozambican government and foreign diplomats.
A statement from the Swiss embassy on Monday said Dannecker was "perplexed and dismayed" by the September 30 murder of anthropologist Nicole Bezencon at Tsalala near the capital Maputo.
Bezencon was killed in broad daylight by car thieves when she was returning from a school belonging to the National Water Board where she gave classes.
Diplomats at the Monday meeting said they wanted a "political signal" from the government indicating its commitment to the fight against crime.
The meeting's spokesman, Swiss charge d'affaires Gregor Binkert, said donor countries were very worried about the crime situation.
"It could have negative effects on the country's economic recovery and on development cooperation programmes," Binkert said.
Binkert added that the donors wanted "concrete and speedy results" from the investigation into Bezencon's murder. No arrests have yet been announced.
Monday's Swiss statement made it clear that the future of Swiss cooperation with Mozambique will depend on firm action.
"In the next few days decisions will be taken in relation to the cooperation programme between Switzerland and Mozambique," the statement said.
